title: On Walking to the far farm before noon
subtitle: 交通出行 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）
meta: 主题语境：交通出行（人与自我·生活与学习·出行与交通）　|　核心词汇：walk　|　正文 356 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 walk 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1975 the foreman ① walked to the far farm before noon without complaint, and every worker in the site said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three shifts on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the foreman ② walks to the far farm before noon with great care without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ walk to the far farm before noon at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ walked to the far farm before noon before — a line in the sheet for May 1969 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Walking to the far farm before noon without complaint, the foreman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the rope at the far ramp, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ walk the old man home every evening with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Walk the old man home every evening at once and never mention it again.

By 1982 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the sheet, and a new worker from the next site ⑧ walks the old man home every evening without complaint every shift without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the ramp, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ walked to the far farm before noon again when nobody else would.

⑩ To walk to the far farm before noon, my mother said in 1987, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the site remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the site forgets, somebody walks to the far farm before noon with great care again and somebody must walk to the far farm before noon without complaint all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 步行（一般过去式 walked to the far farm before noon：1975 年工头头一回这样做，毫无怨言地）
B. v. 步行（一般现在 walks to the far farm before noon：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 步行（不定式 to walk to the far farm before noon：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 步行（过去完成时 had walked to the far farm before noon：1969 年五月的施工单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 步行（动名词 walking to the far farm before noon 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 陪…走（walk the old man home every evening：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去陪…走每晚陪那位老人走回家）
G. v. 陪…走（walk the old man home every evening：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 步行（后段两处：新来的工人照例 walks the old man home every evening，而母亲又一次 walked to the far farm before noon）

answers.why: walk 意为“步行”，1975 年工头毫无怨言地步行午前走到最远那个农庄，那是工地里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 walked。
walk 意为“步行”，自那以后工头小心翼翼地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 walks。
walk 意为“步行”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯步行午前走到最远那个农庄”，此处为不定式 to walk to the far farm before noon。
walk 意为“步行”，施工单里 五月 那行字说明早在 1982 年之前就有人步行过，故用过去完成时 had walked。
walk 意为“步行”，工头说“步行午前走到最远那个农庄这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 walking to the far farm before noon 作主语。
walk 意为“陪…走”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去陪…走每晚陪那位老人走回家”，should ever 之后用原形 walk the old man home every evening。
walk 意为“陪…走”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻陪…走每晚陪那位老人走回家（walk the old man home every evening at once），以后再也不要提起。
walk 意为“步行”，新来的工人每个班次都照例陪…走每晚陪那位老人走回家，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 walks。
walk 意为“步行”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次毫无怨言地步行午前走到最远那个农庄，用一般过去式 walked 叙述。
walk 意为“步行”，结尾那句是母亲 1987 年的话：要步行午前走到最远那个农庄，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和工地记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 walk 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1975 the foreman walked to the far farm before noon without complaint, and nobody in the site forgot it.
Even now the foreman walks to the far farm before noon with great care whenever the site asks.
Walking to the far farm before noon without complaint, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever walk the old man home every evening with great care, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new worker from the next site walks the old man home every evening without complaint every shift, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother walked to the far farm before noon again, and the site remembered that half.
